stem.en: The term biodiversity was popularised by:

explanation.en: NCERT: the sociobiologist Edward Wilson popularised the term.

stem.en: Variation in the potency and concentration of reserpine in Rauwolfia vomitoria from different Himalayan ranges is an example of:

explanation.en: One species showing variation over its range is genetic diversity.

stem.en: India's share of the world's land area and of global species diversity are respectively:

explanation.en: India has 2.4% of the land area but 8.1% of global species diversity.

stem.en: According to Robert May, the global species diversity is about:

explanation.en: May's estimate is about 7 million; about 1.5 million have been described.

solution.en: May's estimate is about 7 million; about 1.5 million have been described.

stem.en: Which statement about global species diversity is correct?

options.en: The number of fungal species is more than the combined total of fishes, amphibians, reptiles and mammals
Plants make up more than 70% of all recorded species
Insects make up less than 20% of animal species
Mammals are the most species-rich group of animals

explanation.en: NCERT states the fungi fact; animals (not plants) exceed 70%, and insects exceed 70% of animals.

stem.en: In general, species diversity:

options.en: increases from the equator towards the poles
is the same at all latitudes
decreases from the equator towards the poles

explanation.en: This is the latitudinal gradient in diversity.

stem.en: The species–area relationship was first described by:

explanation.en: Humboldt observed it during his explorations of South American jungles.

stem.en: In the equation log S = log C + Z log A, Z represents:

options.en: the slope of the line (regression coefficient)

explanation.en: S = species richness, A = area, C = Y-intercept, Z = slope.

stem.en: For very large areas such as entire continents, the value of Z in the species–area relationship lies in the range:

explanation.en: Z is 0.1–0.2 for most regions but 0.6–1.2 for very large areas like continents.

solution.en: Z is 0.1–0.2 for most regions but 0.6–1.2 for very large areas like continents.

stem.en: If Z = 0.2 for a region, increasing the area surveyed 1,024 times will increase the number of species:
The "rivet popper hypothesis" was proposed by:

explanation.en: Stanford ecologist Paul Ehrlich proposed it.

stem.en: The most important cause of animal and plant extinction is:

explanation.en: NCERT: habitat loss and fragmentation is the most important cause.

stem.en: The introduction of the Nile perch into Lake Victoria led to the extinction of more than 200 species of:

explanation.en: Nile perch caused the extinction of an ecologically unique assemblage of over 200 cichlid fish species.

stem.en: David Tilman's long-term ecosystem experiments showed that plots with more species:

options.en: showed more year-to-year variation in total biomass
were more easily invaded by alien species
showed less year-to-year variation in total biomass

explanation.en: More species gave more stable (less variable) and higher productivity.

solution.en: More species gave more stable (less variable) and higher productivity.

stem.en: According to the IUCN Red List (2004), the number of species that became extinct in the last 500 years is:

explanation.en: 784 extinctions: 338 vertebrates, 359 invertebrates and 87 plants.

stem.en: Which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?

explanation.en: The thylacine was from Australia; the dodo was from Mauritius.

stem.en: Exploring molecular, genetic and species-level diversity for products of economic importance is called:

explanation.en: NCERT defines this as bioprospecting.

stem.en: The Amazon forest is estimated to produce what percentage of the total oxygen in the Earth's atmosphere through photosynthesis?

explanation.en: NCERT: about 20 per cent.

stem.en: Pollination of crops by bees and bats is an argument for conservation that is:

explanation.en: Ecosystem services such as pollination form the broadly utilitarian argument.

stem.en: More than what percentage of drugs currently sold in the market worldwide are derived from plants?

explanation.en: NCERT: more than 25 per cent of drugs are derived from plants.

solution.en: NCERT: more than 25 per cent of drugs are derived from plants.

stem.en: The ethical argument for conserving biodiversity is based on the idea that:

options.en: every species has an intrinsic value, even if it has no current economic value to us

explanation.en: Ethical arguments rest on the intrinsic value of species and our moral duty to them.

stem.en: The criteria for identifying biodiversity hotspots are:

options.en: low species richness and high endemism
high human population and high species richness
high levels of species richness and a high degree of endemism

explanation.en: Hotspots have very high species richness and high endemism.

stem.en: Which of the following is an ex situ method of conservation?

explanation.en: Seed banks store material outside the natural habitat; the others protect habitats in situ.

stem.en: Which of these is NOT one of the biodiversity hotspots covering India?

explanation.en: India's hotspots are the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and the Himalaya.

stem.en: In Meghalaya, sacred groves in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills are important because they:

options.en: are the last refuges for a large number of rare and threatened plants
are seed banks for crop plants

explanation.en: NCERT: the sacred groves of Meghalaya are the last refuges for many rare and threatened plants.

solution.en: NCERT: the sacred groves of Meghalaya are the last refuges for many rare and threatened plants.

stem.en: The total number of biodiversity hotspots in the world, and the approximate share of the Earth's land area they cover together, are:

explanation.en: Initially 25, then 9 more added (34); together they cover less than 2% of the land area.

stem.en: The World Summit on Sustainable Development, at which 190 countries pledged to significantly reduce the rate of biodiversity loss by 2010, was held in:

explanation.en: Rio (1992) was the Earth Summit; the 2002 follow-up was in Johannesburg, South Africa.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Tropical regions have greater species diversity than temperate regions.
Reason (R): Tropical environments are less seasonal and relatively more constant and predictable than temperate ones.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: NCERT: a constant, predictable environment promotes niche specialisation and leads to greater species diversity.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The introduction of the Nile perch into Lake Victoria led to the extinction of more than 200 species of cichlid fish.
Reason (R): Every alien species introduced into a new habitat becomes invasive.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true (NCERT); but not every introduced species becomes invasive; only some do, and they then cause decline or extinction of native species.

passage.en: An ecologist counts plant species in nested plots of increasing area within one region of the Western Ghats. She plots log S (species) against log A (area) and gets a straight line with slope Z = 0.25. She then plans to extend the same study to compare much larger areas, such as whole continents.

stem.en: According to her results, if the area surveyed is increased 16 times, the number of species will:

explanation.en: S = C·A^Z, so S increases by 16^0.25 = 2 times.

passage.en: An ecologist counts plant species in nested plots of increasing area within one region of the Western Ghats. She plots log S (species) against log A (area) and gets a straight line with slope Z = 0.25. She then plans to extend the same study to compare much larger areas, such as whole continents.

stem.en: When she compares very large areas such as whole continents, the slope Z is expected to be:

explanation.en: NCERT: for very large areas such as entire continents, the slope of the species–area line is much steeper, 0.6–1.2.

stem.en: For a group of organisms in a region, C = 4 and Z = 0.2 in the species–area relationship S = CA^Z. How many species are expected in an area of 3,125 km²?

Consider the statements:
I. On a logarithmic scale the species–area relationship is a straight line: log S = log C + Z log A.
II. For most regions, Z lies between 0.1 and 0.2 regardless of the taxonomic group.
III. For very large areas such as whole continents, the slope is much steeper (Z = 0.6 to 1.2).
IV. Species diversity increases from the equator towards the poles.
Which statements are correct?

explanation.en: IV is wrong: diversity decreases from the equator towards the poles (latitudinal gradient).

stem.en:
Match each case in Column I with its cause of biodiversity loss in Column II.
Column I: (a) Nile perch in Lake Victoria (b) Steller's sea cow (c) clearing of the Amazon forest for soya beans and cattle (d) a parasite dying out with its host fish
Column II: (i) habitat loss (ii) co-extinction (iii) alien species invasion (iv) over-exploitation

explanation.en: The introduced Nile perch wiped out over 200 cichlid species (alien species); Steller's sea cow was hunted out (over-exploitation); Amazon clearing is habitat loss; a host-specific parasite dies with its host (co-extinction).

solution.en: The introduced Nile perch wiped out over 200 cichlid species (alien species); Steller's sea cow was hunted out (over-exploitation); Amazon clearing is habitat loss; a host-specific parasite dies with its host (co-extinction).

stem.en: Which statement about recent extinctions is correct according to the IUCN Red List (2004)?

options.en: Most of the recorded extinctions are of plants
Present extinction rates are only 10 to 20 times the pre-human rates
The dodo and the quagga still survive in zoos
784 species became extinct in 500 years: 338 vertebrates, 359 invertebrates and 87 plants

explanation.en: 338 + 359 + 87 = 784 extinctions in the last 500 years; current rates are estimated at 100 to 1,000 times the pre-human rate, and the dodo and quagga are extinct.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Tropical latitudes have greater species diversity than temperate latitudes.
Reason (R): Tropical environments are highly seasonal and unpredictable, which promotes niche specialisation.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true. R is false: tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable, which is one reason they hold more species.

stem.en: The term 'biodiversity' was popularised by the sociobiologist:

explanation.en: Edward Wilson popularised the term to describe the combined diversity at all levels of biological organisation. Robert May estimated global species numbers, Ehrlich proposed the rivet popper hypothesis and Humboldt the species–area relationship.

stem.en: India has only 2.4 per cent of the world's land area. Its share of the global species diversity is:

explanation.en: India's share of global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent — one reason it is one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world.

stem.en: India is one of the ______ mega diversity countries of the world.

explanation.en: NCERT: India is one of the 12 mega diversity countries. 34 is the number of biodiversity hotspots; 25 the original number of hotspots.

stem.en: The medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria growing in different Himalayan ranges shows variation in the potency and concentration of the chemical reserpine. This is an example of:

explanation.en: Variation within a single species (here in the active chemical it produces) over its distributional range is genetic diversity.

stem.en: According to the IUCN (2004), the total number of plant and animal species described so far is:

explanation.en: IUCN (2004): slightly more than 1.5 million species described. Robert May's global estimate of all species (described + undescribed) is about 7 million.

stem.en: Robert May places the global species diversity at about:

explanation.en: Robert May's estimate, using the ratio of described temperate to tropical species, is about 7 million. Many earlier estimates ranged from 20 to 50 million.

stem.en: The total number of biodiversity hotspots in the world at present is:

explanation.en: Initially 25 biodiversity hotspots were identified; subsequently nine more were added, bringing the total to 34.

stem.en: The dodo, a famous example of recent extinction, belonged to:

explanation.en: Dodo — Mauritius; quagga — Africa; thylacine — Australia; Steller's sea cow — Russia.

stem.en: In India, sacred groves are found in several regions. In Meghalaya they are found in the:

explanation.en: Sacred groves: Khasi and Jaintia Hills (Meghalaya), Aravalli Hills (Rajasthan), Western Ghat regions of Karnataka and Maharashtra, and Sarguja, Chanda and Bastar areas (Madhya Pradesh).

stem.en: The historic Convention on Biological Diversity ('The Earth Summit') was held in 1992 at:

explanation.en: The Earth Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992. The World Summit on Sustainable Development was held in Johannesburg in 2002.

stem.en: The introduction of the Nile perch led to the extinction of more than 200 species of cichlid fish in:

explanation.en: When the Nile perch was introduced into Lake Victoria in east Africa, it eventually led to the extinction of an ecologically unique assemblage of more than 200 species of cichlid fish — an alien species invasion.

stem.en: Among animals, insects are the most species-rich taxonomic group. Approximately how many out of every 10 animals on this planet are insects?

explanation.en: Insects make up more than 70 per cent of all recorded animal species, i.e. about 7 out of every 10 animals.

stem.en: India has more than ____ genetically different strains of rice and ____ varieties of mango.

explanation.en: NCERT: India has more than 50,000 genetically different strains of rice and 1,000 varieties of mango — examples of genetic diversity.

stem.en: The Western Ghats have a greater amphibian species diversity than the Eastern Ghats. This illustrates:

explanation.en: Diversity at the species level (number of amphibian species in two regions) is species diversity.

stem.en: India, with its deserts, rain forests, mangroves, coral reefs, wetlands, estuaries and alpine meadows, has greater ______ than a Scandinavian country like Norway.

explanation.en: Diversity at the ecosystem level — the variety of ecosystem types — is ecological diversity.

stem.en: As an example of the latitudinal gradient in diversity, Colombia, located near the equator, has nearly how many species of birds?

explanation.en: Colombia has nearly 1,400 bird species; New York at 41° N has 105 and Greenland at 71° N only 56. India, with much of its land in the tropics, has more than 1,200.

stem.en: The Amazonian rain forest in South America has the greatest biodiversity on Earth. It is home to more than ______ species of plants.

explanation.en: Amazon: more than 40,000 species of plants, 3,000 of fishes, 1,300 of birds, 427 of mammals, 427 of amphibians, 378 of reptiles and more than 1,25,000 invertebrates.

stem.en: The species–area relationship — species richness increases with increasing explored area, but only up to a limit — was observed by the German naturalist:

explanation.en: During his extensive explorations in the wildernesses of South American jungles, Alexander von Humboldt observed this relationship.

stem.en: In the species–area relationship, the value of Z (slope of the line) generally lies in the range of:

explanation.en: Ecologists have found that Z values lie in the range 0.1 to 0.2, regardless of the taxonomic group or the region. For very large areas such as entire continents, the slope is much steeper (0.6–1.2).

stem.en: For frugivorous (fruit-eating) birds and mammals in the tropical forests of different continents, the slope Z of the species–area line is:

explanation.en: NCERT: for frugivorous birds and mammals in tropical forests of different continents, the slope is found to be 1.15 — a steep slope typical of very large areas.

stem.en: The 'rivet popper hypothesis', an analogy explaining the importance of each species to ecosystem function, was proposed by:

explanation.en: Stanford ecologist Paul Ehrlich compared an ecosystem to an aeroplane and species to rivets; losing rivets (species) may not affect flight safety at first, but as more are lost the plane becomes dangerously weak. Losing rivets on the wings (key species) is more serious than losing a few on the seats.

stem.en: David Tilman's long-term ecosystem experiments using outdoor plots showed that plots with more species:

explanation.en: Tilman found that plots with more species showed less year-to-year variation in total biomass, and that increased diversity contributed to higher productivity.

options.en: Had greater year-to-year variation in total biomass
Showed less year-to-year variation in total biomass

stem.en: According to the IUCN Red List (2004), the number of species documented to have become extinct in the last 500 years is:

explanation.en: 784 extinctions: 338 vertebrates, 359 invertebrates and 87 plants. 15,500 is the number of species currently facing the threat of extinction.

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT one of the four major causes of biodiversity loss ('The Evil Quartet')?

explanation.en: The Evil Quartet: habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions. Mutualism is a beneficial interaction, not a cause of loss.

stem.en: Tropical rain forests once covered 14 per cent of the Earth's land surface. Now they cover:

explanation.en: Tropical rain forests now cover no more than 6 per cent — a dramatic example of habitat loss. They are being destroyed fast, and many species living in them face extinction.

stem.en: The Amazon rain forest, called the 'lungs of the planet', is being cut and cleared mainly for:

explanation.en: NCERT: the Amazon rain forest harbouring probably millions of species is being cut and cleared for cultivating soya beans or for conversion to grasslands for raising beef cattle.

options.en: Cultivating soya beans or conversion to grasslands for raising beef cattle

stem.en: The extinction of Steller's sea cow and the passenger pigeon in the last 500 years was mainly due to:

explanation.en: When biological need turns into greed, it leads to over-exploitation of natural resources. Many species extinctions in the last 500 years (Steller's sea cow, passenger pigeon) were due to over-exploitation by humans.

stem.en: The illegal introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus for aquaculture purposes is posing a threat to:

explanation.en: NCERT: the recent illegal introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus for aquaculture is posing a threat to the indigenous catfishes in our rivers. Cichlids of Lake Victoria were affected by the Nile perch.

options.en: The indigenous catfishes in Indian rivers

stem.en: When a host fish species becomes extinct, its unique assemblage of parasites also meets the same fate. This is an example of:

explanation.en: When a species becomes extinct, the plant and animal species associated with it in an obligatory way also become extinct — co-extinction. A plant–pollinator mutualism is another case.

stem.en: The Amazon forest is estimated to produce, through photosynthesis, about 20 per cent of the total oxygen in the Earth's atmosphere. Conserving biodiversity for such services is a:

explanation.en: Broadly utilitarian arguments are about ecosystem services such as oxygen production, pollination and aesthetic pleasure. Narrowly utilitarian arguments concern direct economic products (food, fibre, medicines); the ethical argument is about the intrinsic value of every species.

stem.en:
How many of the following are biodiversity hotspots that cover India's ecologically rich regions?
Western Ghats and Sri Lanka; Indo-Burma; Himalaya; Thar desert; Sundarbans; Deccan plateau

explanation.en: Three of the 34 hotspots cover India's rich biodiversity regions — Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and Himalaya. The others are not hotspots.

stem.en: On a log–log plot of the species–area relationship, log S = log C + Z log A. Here Z represents:

explanation.en: On a logarithmic scale the relationship is a straight line, log S = log C + Z log A, where S = species richness, A = area, C = Y-intercept and Z = slope of the line (regression coefficient).

options.en: The slope of the line (regression coefficient)

stem.en: For a group of islands, species richness follows S = C A^Z with Z = 0.2. If one island is 32 times larger in area than another, its species richness is expected to be greater by a factor of:

explanation.en: S₂/S₁ = (A₂/A₁)^Z = 32^0.2 = (2⁵)^0.2 = 2. 6.4 = 32 × 0.2 multiplies instead of raising to the power; 32 assumes Z = 1.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Tropical latitudes harbour more species than temperate or polar areas.
Reason (R): Unlike temperate regions subjected to frequent glaciations, tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, giving a long evolutionary time for species diversification.

explanation.en: R is one of the NCERT hypotheses explaining the latitudinal gradient (others: less seasonal, more predictable environment; more solar energy giving higher productivity). It explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en:
Statement I: Tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable, which promotes niche specialisation and greater species diversity.
Statement II: Less solar energy is available in the tropics, which leads to lower productivity.

explanation.en: Statement I is an NCERT hypothesis. Statement II is wrong: there is MORE solar energy available in the tropics, contributing to higher productivity, which in turn might contribute indirectly to greater diversity.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en:
Match List I (extinct animal) with List II (region).
List I: (P) Dodo (Q) Quagga (R) Thylacine (S) Steller's sea cow
List II: (1) Russia (2) Australia (3) Mauritius (4) Africa

explanation.en: Dodo — Mauritius; quagga — Africa; thylacine (Tasmanian wolf) — Australia; Steller's sea cow — Russia. Three subspecies of tiger (Bali, Javan, Caspian) are other recent extinctions.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Although all biodiversity hotspots together cover less than 2 per cent of the Earth's land area, their strict protection could reduce the ongoing mass extinctions by almost 30 per cent.
Reason (R): Hotspots are regions with very high levels of species richness and a high degree of endemism.

explanation.en: Because hotspots concentrate an enormous number of species, including many found nowhere else (endemics), protecting this small area protects a large share of global species — R explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en:
Statement I: Biosphere reserves, national parks and wildlife sanctuaries are examples of in situ conservation.
Statement II: India now has 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks and 448 wildlife sanctuaries.

explanation.en: Both are NCERT statements. Protected areas conserve species in their natural habitat — in situ conservation.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en:
Match List I (group) with List II (percentage of its species facing the threat of extinction, as given in NCERT).
List I: (P) Birds (Q) Mammals (R) Amphibians (S) Gymnosperms
List II: (1) 31% (2) 23% (3) 12% (4) 32%

explanation.en: Presently 12 per cent of all bird species, 23 per cent of mammals, 32 per cent of amphibians and 31 per cent of gymnosperm species face the threat of extinction.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The current (sixth) mass extinction is proceeding at about the same rate as the previous five episodes.
Reason (R): The current rates of extinction are estimated to be 100 to 1000 times faster than in pre-human times, and human activities are responsible.

explanation.en: A is false and R is true. NCERT: the 'Sixth Extinction' presently in progress is different from the previous episodes in that it is 100 to 1000 times faster, and we humans are responsible for the faster rates.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en:
Statement I: At the World Summit on Sustainable Development held in 2002 in Johannesburg, 190 countries pledged to achieve a significant reduction in the current rate of biodiversity loss by 2010.
Statement II: The Earth Summit of 1992 was held in Johannesburg.

explanation.en: Statement I is correct. Statement II is wrong: the 1992 Earth Summit (Convention on Biological Diversity) was held in Rio de Janeiro.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en:
How many of the following are effects of loss of biodiversity in a region, as given in NCERT?
(i) decline in plant production; (ii) lowered resistance to environmental perturbations such as drought; (iii) increased variability in ecosystem processes such as plant productivity, water use, and pest and disease cycles; (iv) increased stability of the ecosystem; (v) increased year-to-year constancy of biomass

explanation.en: (i), (ii) and (iii) are the NCERT effects. (iv) and (v) are the opposite — loss of diversity reduces stability and increases year-to-year variation (Tilman).
